title: TEXTJOIN: join a range and skip blanks

screens.prompt: In B7, join the departments in B2:B6 into one line, separated by a comma and a space, skipping the blanks.

hints.syntax: TEXTJOIN takes the separator, whether to skip blanks, then the range: =TEXTJOIN(", ",TRUE,B2:B6).
hints.func-textjoin: TEXTJOIN is the one function that takes a separator and a blank rule; CONCAT would glue everything into one word.
hints.require-ref: Join B2:B6 so a department typed into a blank row is picked up.
hints.value: Three of the five rows hold a department, and they are joined by a comma and a space.
hints.error: TEXTJOIN itself does not error on blanks; string arithmetic on its result does, which is where #VALUE! comes from.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing joins
glues the departments into EngineeringResearchOps with no separators
keeping blanks leaves two empty slots in the line
the departments are separated by spaces instead of commas
the range stops one row short, so Ops is missing
the departments typed into the formula, so a reassignment never reaches the line
concatenating a string with a division by zero returns #VALUE!

docs.explain: Two of the five rows have no department, and a list with ', ,' in the middle reads like a mistake. TEXTJOIN's second argument is the blank rule: TRUE skips empty cells, FALSE keeps them and leaves the separator behind. The first argument is the separator itself, typed as text in quotes —", " means a comma and a space. CONCAT has neither argument, which is why it produces one long unreadable word and cannot be adjusted afterwards. Because the separator is an argument, changing a comma list into a semicolon list, or a space-separated line into something a database can read, is one character in one cell rather than an afternoon of retyping.

errors.text: The joined text was used in arithmetic, which a string cannot do.
TEXTJOIN was typed without its last letter, so the sheet sees a name it does not know.

docs.atWork: Building a summary line from a column of tags, roles or categories where some rows are empty.
docs.outcome: Join a column into one line and choose what happens to the blanks.
